claims.text: Ti3SiC2 is a layered MAX-phase material.
Optimized Ti3SiC2 can combine high mechanical strength with intrinsic self-lubricating behavior.
The proposed Ti3SiC2 material can retain this combination across a wide temperature range.
Ti3SiC2 has an inherent laminated microstructure and a load-bearing ceramic framework.
Controlled powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering can enhance the load-bearing matrix and lubricious layered structure.
The proposed material may operate from room temperature to temperatures potentially above 1000 °C.
The proposed material can operate under high mechanical loading typical of extreme environments.
The laminated microstructure of Ti3SiC2 promotes interlayer sliding.
Interlayer sliding produces intrinsic self-lubrication through easy shear.
Easy interlayer shear lowers friction and reduces wear.
A dense ceramic matrix provides high mechanical strength.
Composition and processing optimization improve interfacial bonding and phase distribution.
Improved interfacial bonding and phase distribution balance lubricity and toughness.
Optimized Ti3SiC2 will maintain low friction and stable wear resistance over the evaluated temperature range.
Optimized Ti3SiC2 will retain mechanical integrity while providing low friction and wear resistance.
Conventional MoS2- or graphite-based self-lubricating systems typically have limited mechanical strength or reduced lubricity at high temperatures.
The proposed benefits require preservation of the layered MAX-phase structure during processing.
Composition deviations or improper sintering may cause phase decomposition or excessive grain growth that degrades strength or lubrication performance.
